background.source: The American Presidential System is one form of government that is adopted by several countries around the world. In this system, the head of government is directly or indirectly elected by a group of citizens and holds the title of president. The president is not responsible to the legislature and is the head of state as well as the head of the executive branch of the government. The presidency term in the United States is restricted to four years, after which the president has to be re-elected for another four-year term if he/she wishes to continue serving as the president. This system of government is prevalent in the mainland Americas, Central and southern West Africa and in Central Asia, and is in contrast to a parliamentary system where the head of government is elected by gaining the confidence of an elected legislature.
background.target: A German Constitutional Monarchy is a form of government in which the monarch exercises their authority in accordance with a constitution and is not alone in decision making. This differs from absolute monarchies where the monarch is the only decision-maker. Constitutional monarchies have a legal framework to exercise their powers and authorities within limits prescribed by the constitution. The monarch may hold formal authority and act as a non-party political head of state under the constitution, but they do not personally set public policy or choose political leaders. This system is also known as a parliamentary monarchy or democratic monarchy. In Germany, the emperor holds a hereditary position with life tenure.
